title: Websites and web apps for mental health practices
meta_description: Creosote Labs builds websites, intake forms, and client portals for mental health practices. Fixed price, quoted after a scoping call.
h1: Website and web application development for mental health practices
intro: Most mental health practices are found through a Psychology Today profile, an insurance directory, or a referral, and the practice website is where a prospective client goes next to check clinician bios, fees, insurance accepted, and how to get started. Many practice sites are a template with a contact form, while intake paperwork, consent forms, and the good-faith estimate are still emailed as PDFs or handled through a client portal that is separate from the site. Website work covers both the marketing site and those client-facing steps.

Creosote Labs builds practice websites with clinician pages, a plain list of services and fees, accepted insurance, and a request-appointment form that routes to the right person. Where the practice wants more, we build the client-facing tools around it: a screening form that asks the questions the front desk asks on the first call, a page that explains what happens after a request, and links that hand off to the SimplePractice or TherapyNotes client portal for scheduling and paperwork. Hosting, the domain, and documentation are part of the handover.
projects: A practice website with a page per clinician listing specialties, license type, session format, and current availability.
A new-client request form that collects concern, insurance, and preferred times and sends a confirmation with next steps and the practice's fee notice.
A services and fees page with a good-faith estimate calculator based on session type and frequency.
A group practice site that lets the office manager add or remove clinicians and update availability without editing code.
A referral form for physicians and schools that submits directly to the intake coordinator's queue.

faqs.q: Can the site handle intake paperwork and scheduling?
faqs.a: It can link to or embed the client portal the practice already uses, such as SimplePractice or TherapyNotes, for signed consents and scheduling. We can also build a screening form on the site itself; anything that collects health information is discussed during scoping so hosting and agreements are set up appropriately.

faqs.q: How much does a practice website cost?
faqs.a: Website and application projects are quoted after a scoping call, at a fixed price with no hourly billing. The quote depends on the number of pages, forms, and integrations.

faqs.q: What does the practice need to provide?
faqs.a: Clinician bios and photos, the fee schedule and insurance list, and access to the domain registrar. We handle hosting setup, domain configuration, and documentation at handover.
